results.title: SM64 Beta Revival Project (Dudaw)
results.description:
I would recommend to edit the save file so all the doors are opened and etc.
Also expect lots of bugs and crashes to happen, since these are unfinished builds of a beta hack  

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Super Mario 64 Beta Revival Project (2/2/13)
https://archive.org/details/sm64brp-february-2013

-This versions contains the Metal Cap switch and 1 star, but I found a discovery where if you hit the Metal Cap switch (don't collect the star from bowser 1) and reset the game you'll get Whomp's Fortress instead of Course 18 (Course 18 is Bowser 3 if you didn't know) leading you to collect 2 stars. I also got a replacement of the Metal Cap area, where it was a checkerboard pattern land with a mama penguin in it asking for you to look for the young (I don't remember the exact dialogue, but I'll update this once I enter it).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Super Mario 64 Beta Revival Project (10/25/16)
https://archive.org/details/sm64brp-2016

-This version contains 5 stars, a map by pressing R, and its all Japanese, so feel free to translate the text. You could also pause the game to select different levels. PJ64 has some problems with it so it only works on Parallel Launcher 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Super Mario 64 Beta Revival Project (7/6/19)
https://archive.org/details/sm64brp-2019

-This one doesn't work sadly, but if you want to fix it, go for it 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

More information about this below:
https://video-game-beta-remakes.fandom.com/wiki/Super_Mario_64_Beta_Revival_(dudaw12)

results.title: Super Mario 64: Plumber To The Past
results.description:
Thank you for trying my rom hack of Super Mario 64 crossed over with Zelda Link To The Past! This demo is only the Light World demo with all areas pretty much finished! There might be some small collision issues in a couple places, but if you run into one try long jumping or flip jumping to get past it!
	
Some models seem a bit off in terms of looks cause well I have no clue, but they function like the model they are supposed to be! 
Not water boxes yet! I have to figure out how to scale them down. Most stars are collectable as I counted 38-39 collectable stars though others ned their trajectory fixed like boss stars.
	
I made many textures myself and ripped and improved others from Zelda LTTP! 
No music added yet as that will be last. If you die just reset the game for now until the death warp is fixed for health recovery. No new text added yet. Look everywhere for secrets and most important...
	
HAVE FUN!
	
From: Wolfblade1989
	
Dark World will be more completed possibly first three dungeons in demo 2!

results.title: Deteriorating World Chapter 1: Alpha Demo [cancelled]
results.description:
Due to overwhelmingly bad reviews based on stylistically how i was building this hack I have decided to cancel this hack, and I will attempt to either rework this or make something completely different

This 26 star demo is a very early look at my biggest project yet. A hack with over 90 levels, 170 stars, and tons of areas and secrets to explore. 

You may notice that not all stars in course 1 are in course 1. That is just a primitive stardisplay thing for me to work out. Course 1 is split into 3 levels seperate levels. A map will be released on final version

As a fair warning as the late stages are added the community might decide this is kaizo. Me and my playtesters will get desensitized to the movement by the time the hack is released, so I am very happy to be overrulled if the final hack turns kaizo, however as it stands this hack is intended to be casual for the time being.

One more thing. You will notice some doors that lead to nowhere. This will be addressed in the final release. I have storyboarded the entire hack already, and it's more a matter of putting it together for the most part with minor changes being introduced

results.title: Cap Challenge Concepts Edition
results.description:
Another Super Mario 64 vanilla edit? Lazy. 2 years of work? Lemme see...

Plugin says OGRE, but I used Jabo because old Project64.

Changes:
-More moves chain together and Mario is a little slower.

-Hopefully fixed sequence breaks. Let me know, experts, I tried really hard, maybe went overboard.

-MOST IMPORTANTLY, more enemies will take Mario's cap and he will have to retrieve it from them. A couple enemies (namely the fish enemies and Bubba) will keep it until leaving the area and you'll find it elsewhere, so beware.

-Mario can also lose his Cap a few other ways, such as hitting walls and falling down.

-A good handful of behavior changes.

-Alternate enemies, one of which you'll find in a secret game mode.

-A Stat/Rank system at the end of the game. Game SAVES at the Grand Star.

-8 extra secret stars.

-Some missions were replaced with new ones.

-40 Bonus Stars for veterans. Unlocks game play choices for New Game.

-Custom ASM results in Expansion Pak requirement.

-Fully tested on real hardware/EverDrive. Only one non-vanilla crash I am aware of, but it seems too rare for me to replicate (related to Klepto dive behavior and Mario collision. Happened only once when Mario was swimming and just barely touched his Cap after Klepto dove in). Other than that, I did my best to prevent the out-of-bounds Mario's Cap crash from being a factor.
(VERSION 1.2 should resolve the crash with Klepto.)

-Also, more Toads. Make sure you read any new signposts too.

-A pipe to delete your saved progress and a fallen star to save the game anytime.

-Only one game file. I needed to make room for extra conditions and stats, etc.

-Anything else I forgot! ...Oh! The intro cutscene is shorter!

Please let me know if the patch worked for you, NTSC users!

EDIT: Version 1.3 should resolve an oversight where if the Mario cap gets swiped while loose sometimes it'll glitch and become uncollectable or not spawn at all. This version will also make an endgame criteria more feasible (timer-related). Also, goombas and scuttlebugs now die in bottomless pits. Goombas slow down while running against the end of a platform. Finally, some other tweaks including a missing behavior for Klepto (oh boy...) and anything else I forgot.
EDIT AGAIN: Version 1.31 fixes a code that changed without my knowledge. This will resolve a problem that would otherwise make Mario permanently capless.

results.title: Super Tyler 64
results.description:
Super Tyler 64 is a color-edited Super Mario 64 ROM hack where Mario has been transformed into Tyler through complete palette adjustments. Mario’s original “M” and colors have been replaced to match Tyler’s look, giving the classic game a fresh visual identity while keeping the original gameplay fully intact. The character model, animations, and movement set remain unchanged to maintain stability and avoid conflict with emulator compatibility.

The HUD was intentionally left unmodified, as previous attempts to alter it caused major system crashes during development. To ensure a smooth and reliable experience, the interface remains in its original form.

Super Tyler 64 has been tested and confirmed to run successfully with several N64 plugins, including:

GLideN64

Jabo’s Direct3D8

Rice

Glide64

Parallel


These plugins offer the best stability. Other setups or unsupported mobile emulators may cause crashes or graphical issues.

Do you like Super Tyler 64?

Yes

No
(Your answer is your personal opinion and helps guide potential future revisions.)


Super Tyler 64 is a simple, clean re-imagining of Mario 64 built entirely by Record64, focusing on visual style over major gameplay changes. It preserves the original experience while giving it a unique Tyler-themed twist.

results.title: Super Mario 66
results.description:
Super Mario 66 is what was once an extremely eager attempt at making an "awesome" and moderately difficult hack way back in 2016. With the little knowledge I had at the time, and for that matter no game-design and storymaking skill, it turned out just as odd as a hack could be. Young me couldn't do much but force in ideas that didn't work out or are straight up absurd. With that said, there are several areas that are left intentionally buggy and some that could crash the game.
A remake is on its way, projected to be released before 2030. I'm giving myself that much time to work on gathering the skills, knowledge and love that for a rom hack named "Super Mario 66" could have (...and working on other small projects along the side).
Additional credits to Crash for the "C-3" level - which I disrespectfully ripped from the Sketchup Workshop, and a huge shoutout to Paudink for the hub design they kindly made me on request. I really wish I could've paid them for that.

results.title: Super Mario 128
results.description:
One of the earliest hacks that remixes the existing levels in Super Mario 64 in evil ways. Known by "pioneers" as the first kaizo hack(in the form of a Toad's Tool 64 edit). A relic of the past if you will... It even pre-dates many other well-known old school hacks from 2009-2012.

Features 53 edited stars as seen in the included Star Display layout. Also, it has some other unchanged stars from vanilla SM64, some of which you may need to progress through this confusing extreme hack. Bowser 2 requires 60 stars to access for instance, and the entry is very specific(shown in video below) with C3 being done after B2 because of needing the pillars for the moat unpounded to clip into the B2 level. C13 Star 3 you could do after as well.

*A Few Important Notes*
- For C11(High-Tide Town), Star 1 & Star 3 are doable without editing the game file through Star Display. However, you will need to add C11 Star 2 to the layout with "edit layout" in Star Display and then "edit file" to acquire Star 2. This opens up the ability to select and do Star 4 & Star 5 missions, which have been proven possible. You can then remove Star 2 from the layout to reflect the final 53 unique stars that are required for proof of beating the game if you like. Unfortunately, just the byproduct of an unfinished game.

- C8 & C9 are some of the vanilla SM64 levels you can find and need to do to have enough stars to unlock the Metal Cap stage where C6 normally is. The door requires 50 stars, or alternatively you can do a BLJ into there starting over near the C7 painting, which requires dying in the basement to get a basement OW red. Convoluted, I know...

- C13 just Star 3 is unique, the Koopa the Quick race. He a fast boi... and sporadic. Can do Star 1 & Star 2 first to unlock it, but they are unchanged & uncounted.

- The Bowser 3 fight isn't possible to complete, but the Bowser 1 & 2 levels+fights are. You have 'beaten' the game when those fights & the 53 changed stars are done. Some of the game's stars are easy but many are quite difficult. Savestate practice is recommended if you want to take on this challenge. Good luck!
